name: Alexander
overview: Alexander was a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted for being a man of high-priestly descent as referenced in Acts 4:6. He is possibly identified as the wealthy brother of Philo according to Farrar, highlighting a status of prominence within his community. His Levitical heritage places him within the priestly lineage descending from Aaron.
namesAndTitles: The name Alexander appears once in the biblical record without an explicit meaning provided. It is simply recognized as a proper name mentioned in Acts 4:6, with no indication that it was given by God or carries special significance within the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Alexander as a descendant of Aaron, affirming his priestly lineage. Beyond this, there are no other family relationships detailed in the biblical text, though tradition suggests a possible connection as the brother of Philo.
scriptureSignificance: Alexander's significance in the New Testament arises from his identity as a man of high-priestly descent, situating him within the religious leadership during the early church period. His mention in Acts 4:6 places him among those opposing the apostles, reflecting the tension between the emerging Christian movement and established Jewish authorities. The possible association with wealth and family prominence further underscores his influential position within the Levitical priesthood.
